underground_mines_meta_description: Underground Mines was a Vintage Story mod that generated huge underground mine networks with ores, loot and danger.
underground_mines_hero_lead: Huge mines beneath your feet. Sometimes a little too huge.
underground_mines_hero_description: A procedural generation mod that filled Vintage Story's underground with connected galleries, ores, loot and creatures. Getting in was the easy part.
underground_mines_generation_title: It did not place a mine. It grew one.
underground_mines_generation_description: The mod combined prepared pieces with generation rules to build a different network in every world. Galleries continued through new chunks and could reach a fairly unreasonable scale.
underground_mines_generation_entrances_d: Mines could announce themselves on the surface or connect to caves. You could also find them the traditional way: digging down and having faith.
underground_mines_generation_galleries_d: Corridors, crossings, turns and shafts were combined procedurally to extend the structure without relying on a closed map.
underground_mines_generation_rooms_descr: Special rooms distributed resources, loot and hostile encounters so exploring the network involved more than following empty tunnels.
underground_mines_network_alt: Distant view of a Vintage Story world revealing a huge mine network generated beneath the terrain
underground_mines_network_caption: Remove the terrain and the whole trick appears: a network crossing mountains, lakes and valleys without asking permission.
underground_mines_world_title: The mine had to feel like part of the world.
underground_mines_world_description: Generation did more than paste structures. It read the terrain context to adapt materials, resources and danger to the place where each mine appeared.
underground_mines_rule_rock: Mine blocks adapted to the local rock type instead of looking as though they had been imported from another world.
underground_mines_rule_ores: Ores respected which deposits could exist in that rock, preserving the game's prospecting logic.
underground_mines_rule_danger: Drifters, locusts and other encounters could occupy galleries and special rooms.
underground_mines_rule_config: Depth, entrances, additional ores and other elements could be adjusted through configuration.
underground_mines_technical_description: The challenge was not drawing a nice tunnel. It was making many pieces connect across chunks, survive saved games and preserve the world's internal logic.
underground_mines_technical_code_title: C# and the Vintage Story API
underground_mines_technical_code_descrip: The mod's logic integrated with world generation to decide where, when and how to create each segment.
underground_mines_technical_schematics_d: Entrances, crossings, shafts, endings and mine variants acted as reusable pieces for composing each network.
underground_mines_technical_world_descri: Saved data allowed structures to continue across chunks and preserved generation decisions when the world was loaded again.
underground_mines_technical_server_descr: Generation ran on the server, so multiplayer worlds could include the mines without installing a client interface.
underground_mines_gallery_title: The scale changes with your point of view.
underground_mines_gallery_description: From inside, it was an abandoned mine. From outside, a tangle of galleries determined to occupy half the map.
underground_mines_gallery_interior_alt: Dark interior of a large mine room generated by Underground Mines in Vintage Story
underground_mines_gallery_network_alt: Aerial view of a Vintage Story world with Underground Mines' extensive underground network visible

power_natural_life_meta_description: Development and maintenance of the Power Natural Life Shopify store during my time at the company.
power_natural_life_hero_lead: Raw materials for industry, with a store built to do the job.
power_natural_life_hero_description: I developed and maintained Power Natural Life's new Shopify store during my time at the company, organising a broad catalogue to make professional browsing and purchasing easier.
power_natural_life_challenge_title: A large catalogue should not feel like a warehouse without aisles.
power_natural_life_challenge_description: The store brings together raw materials for businesses in very different sectors. The challenge was not simply publishing products: it was giving them a clear structure and making sure finding, understanding and buying them did not require a map.
power_natural_life_challenge_catalog_des: The structure had to accommodate a broad catalogue without turning navigation into an endless list.
power_natural_life_challenge_professiona: The experience had to support both specific enquiries and recurring business orders.
power_natural_life_challenge_information: Every product needs to present its characteristics, formats and useful documentation clearly enough to support a purchasing decision.
power_natural_life_challenge_maintenance: Products, content and offers change. The store needed to be updated without dismantling its structure every week.
power_natural_life_inside_title: The website was not developed in a bubble.
power_natural_life_inside_description_1: I worked at Power Natural Life from February to October 2026. During that time I created and maintained the new Shopify store, gaining first-hand knowledge of the catalogue, commercial needs and real customer questions.
power_natural_life_inside_description_2: I also managed Amazon Seller Central and helped prepare orders, label products and run warehouse operations. Seeing the full process makes it much easier not to design a store that only works on screen. Real-world details.
power_natural_life_role_store: Creation and maintenance of the new Shopify store.
power_natural_life_role_amazon: Catalogue and operational management in Amazon Seller Central.
power_natural_life_role_operations: Support with order preparation, labelling and warehouse operations.
power_natural_life_technical_title: A foundation ready to sell and keep growing.
power_natural_life_technical_description: The important part was leaving behind a store that worked day to day: clear for buyers and manageable for the people maintaining the catalogue behind it.
power_natural_life_technical_shopify_des: Products, content, customers, orders and checkout live in a platform the team can manage.
power_natural_life_technical_structure_d: Collections, categories and navigation organise very different raw materials without requiring visitors to know every exact product name beforehand.
power_natural_life_technical_purchase_de: Search, product pages, basket and account form a coherent journey that adapts to mobile devices.
power_natural_life_technical_maintenance: The structure allows products, information and campaigns to be updated without rebuilding the store whenever the business changes.

home_meta_title: XurxoMF | Web and Software Developer and IT Technician
home_meta_description: Web development, bespoke software and on-site IT support for businesses and individuals in Salvaterra de Miño and southern Galicia.
home_hero_lead: Useful, well-made software without the smoke and mirrors.
home_hero_description: I am a freelance web and software developer based in Salvaterra de Miño. I build websites, mobile and desktop apps, bots, scripts and automation for businesses and individuals. I also provide remote and on-site IT support across southern Galicia. Yes, sometimes it only needed turning off and on again; but you still had to know that.
home_about_title: From the first idea to a project that actually works.
home_about_paragraph_1: I have spent five years doing this: three working and two training and building my own projects. By the time I started my advanced diploma, I already had Node.js, Discord bots and a fair few hours of wrestling with code behind me.
home_about_paragraph_2: What I enjoy most is watching an idea appear from nowhere, take shape and help a business grow. A website, shop or program should not merely look good in a portfolio: it should be useful in the real world.
home_about_paragraph_3: I try to be as clear with clients as I am with code: if I can do it, I say so; if I do not know or it is not worth your money, I say that too. I explain every decision without jargon and give businesses and individuals the same care. And I do not stop until everything works and looks as it should. Pixel perfect, or I will not sleep soundly.
home_career_description: From systems administration to web development, by way of technical support, e-commerce and agency work. It all comes together in my freelance work now; knowing why something breaks is rather useful when you want to build it properly.
home_services_description: From a website that works for you to a computer that has decided not to cooperate. Development, automation and technical support explained without the hieroglyphics.
home_service_area: I work remotely with clients anywhere and provide on-site IT support in Salvaterra de Miño, Salceda de Caselas, Vigo, O Porriño, Tui, Ponteareas and other parts of Galicia. For businesses and individuals alike.
home_projects_title: Work that does more than look pretty.
home_projects_description: Websites, applications and tools built to solve real problems. I will explain the challenge, the solution and the outcome; the acronyms can wait.
projects_meta_description: A complete selection of websites, applications, automation and software solutions developed by Xurxo MF.
projects_description: Websites, applications and tools made to solve real problems. No alphabet soup, and no calling a button colour change a case study.

aser_audience_workers_description: Courses to update knowledge, improve skills and keep moving forward without having to put your entire life on pause.
aser_audience_companies_description: Subsidised training and tailored programmes, with the management needed to keep training the team from becoming another full-time job.

aser_development_architecture_descriptio: Navigation starts from who arrives and what they need: finding training, improving professionally, or building a team. Less org chart; more answers.
aser_audiences_description: The landing page does not require knowing program names, calls for proposals, or administrative acronyms in advance. First it asks who you are. Then it takes you to what can help you. It seems obvious, which is why sometimes you have to do it.
aser_companies_description: The business area offers subsidized training, customized courses, and comprehensive management as a core service, not just a footnote. In-person or online, depending on what each team needs.
aser_development_theme_description: The AserGalicia identity becomes a custom theme, responsive on mobile and ready for the centre to manage its content.

aser_hero_alt: Screenshot of the AserGalicia Formación home page
aser_development_services_description: Courses, virtual campus, employment, contact and information for companies coexist on the same path without looking like five websites glued together with tape.
aser_companies_title: The team can also be the students.
aser_development_content_description: The structure supports new calls and information without relying on a front page with fixed data that becomes outdated the following quarter.
aser_development_description: The important thing was not to make a huge front page. It was to leave a structure in which each person could find their next step and the center could keep publishing without dismantling it.

gallaecia_desktop_title: Arch to work and live in
gallaecia_editable_description: Arch is in view, as it should be.
gallaecia_gallery_description: Noctalia maintains a consistent palette on the desktop and regenerates it when the theme changes.
gallaecia_desktop_description: Hyprland, Noctalia, greetd, XDG portals, multimedia and a selection of applications chosen during installation. The essentials to get started; the rest is up to you.
gallaecia_gallery_title: Light, dark and whatever the background requires.
gallaecia_gallery_light_alt: Gallaecia Dots desktop with light theme
gallaecia_gallery_dark_alt: Gallaecia Dots desktop with dark theme
gallaecia_desktop_point_3: Applications and defaults à la carte
gallaecia_hero_lead: Arch on desktop or server. In Galician. Without setting up another distribution on top.
gallaecia_code_footer: The release branch is the source of installations; main remains for development.
gallaecia_install_description: The installer prepares the minimum requirements, downloads the stable branch and guides the choice of mode, categories and applications.
gallaecia_hero_description: A set of dotfiles and an interactive installer to give you a small, updatable base that's easy to make your own. Because installing everything "just in case" is also a configuration. Just a worse one.
gallaecia_minimal_title: Install a base. It doesn't decide your whole life.
gallaecia_language_description: The installer, the settings themselves and the desktop use Galician as the main language. When an application does not offer it, the system tries Spanish and then English.
gallaecia_modes_title: The same installer knows when a screen is not needed.
gallaecia_minimal_description: Gallaecia installs the essentials first, then lets you choose the tools that interest you in each category. Repeated packages are installed only once, and applications can be set as default.
gallaecia_process_description: The new installations receive the current base. The existing ones only execute migrations that are not yet recorded, keeping the configuration controlled by the project separate from personal changes.
gallaecia_modes_description: The selected mode persists on the system. Each installation and update applies only the packages, configurations and categories that correspond to it.
gallaecia_meta_description: Gallaecia Dots prepares Arch Linux as a desktop with Hyprland and Noctalia or as a server managed via terminal and SSH, with an interactive installer in Galician.
gallaecia_server_description: A base set up for terminal and SSH, with no graphical stack or desktop packages. Editor, administration, files, deployment, and network, according to what you choose.
gallaecia_process_title: An installation that recalls what has already been done.
gallaecia_step_mode_description: Desktop or server. The choice is saved and subsequent runs respect it.
gallaecia_step_tools_description: You select apps by category and, where applicable, which will be the default one.
gallaecia_step_core_description: Gallaecia prepares only the common base and the mandatory components of the chosen mode.
gallaecia_step_updates_description: Existing installations only apply pending changes, in order and without repeating what has already been done.
gallaecia_terminal_alt: Gallaecia Dots running updates and selecting packages from a clear terminal interface
gallaecia_language_title: The system can also speak like us.
liporca_brand_title: The website had to live up to it.
gallaecia_terminal_caption: Interactive flows with Gum, without making you memorize a novel of commands.
liporca_brand_kicker: The brand already had a voice
liporca_brand_description_2: The development work turned the What The Flow design into a functional, mobile-responsive WordPress theme, set up to manage the catalogue with WooCommerce.
liporca_development_description: The visible part maintains the character of the design. The invisible one handles the catalogue, purchases, languages and all those things that are only remembered when they fail.
liporca_brand_description_1: Liporca was created to free Galician liqueurs from a dated image and bring them to a new generation. That called for a visual, direct and irreverent website, but also a clear shop where people could find the product and buy it without jumping through hoops.
liporca_development_hidden_description: Age verification, contact form, cookies, and complete legal pages make up a website that's ready to operate, not just for show.
liporca_development_languages_descriptio: The experience is available in Galician and Spanish, keeping the structure, navigation, and content coordinated.
liporca_development_shop_description: WooCommerce supports products, cart, account, and checkout process without breaking the website's editorial flow.
liporca_development_title: A brand website that also knows how to work.
liporca_experience_title: From the first visit to the order.
liporca_development_theme_description: The design did not fit into a generic template: it turned into a custom theme, responsive and true to the brand's identity.
liporca_experience_description: Navigation introduces the story and products before taking visitors to the shop. Account, cart and payment sit alongside the editorial content, while contact, cookie consent and age verification complete the business requirements.
liporca_meta_description: Web development and online store for Liporca: a custom WordPress theme with WooCommerce, Galician and Spanish, age verification and legal compliance.
liporca_hero_alt: The four Liporca bottles: cream liqueur, coffee liqueur, herbal liqueur and grape pomace spirit
modereta_arch_data_description: PostgreSQL and Drizzle store drops, series, characters and favourites with reproducible migrations and typed queries.
modereta_arch_commands_description: Slash commands and context menus are loaded, validated and synchronised with Discord from a common manager.
liporca_hero_description: A Galician liqueur brand that decided to speak to its generation without giving up the product it's always made. The website had to do exactly the same: sell, tell the story, and not sound like the brochure for a rural guesthouse.
liporca_toast_alt: Four people toasting with the four liqueurs of Liporca
modereta_arch_deploy_description: Docker Compose brings together the bot and database; continuous integration checks formatting, linting, types and tests before accepting anything.
modereta_delivery_description: The new foundation includes containers for the bot and PostgreSQL, data migrations, command synchronisation and a suite of automated checks. Because “it runs on my machine” is information, not a production strategy.
modereta_demo_description: A sample of the flow, not a screenshot of the bot.
modereta_arch_rules_description: Behaviours that react to other bots live separately from commands. This lets Modereta listen without turning the main file into a mess.
modereta_demo_notice_description: Only people who saved this series or character will be mentioned.
modereta_flow_notify_title: Alert when there is a match
modereta_flow_kicker: A list, a drop, a notice
modereta_flow_notify_description: If anything saved as a favourite shows up, it groups the matches and mentions only the interested people.
modereta_delivery_kicker: It doesn't only work on my laptop
modereta_flow_save_title: Save what you are looking for
modereta_flow_save_description: Each person can maintain a list of favourite series and characters through commands with autocomplete.
modereta_flow_description: People only choose their favourites. Modereta reads Sofi's messages, normalises the names, cross-references the data and sends the alert when needed. The invisible work is the whole point.
modereta_flow_watch_description: A passive rule detects the drops of another bot, interprets the cards, and saves series, characters, and context.
modereta_rewrite_title: The same name. A base that is no longer scary to touch.
modereta_hero_lead: A bot that watches the drops so you do not have to keep staring at the chat.
modereta_hero_description: Modereta is a private bot that integrates with Sofi on Discord: it remembers favourites, understands which cards have appeared and notifies those who are interested. No general spam or clandestine spreadsheets.
modereta_meta_description: Modereta is a private Discord bot rewritten with Bun, TypeScript, PostgreSQL and Drizzle to detect Sofi drops, manage favourites and notify people about matches.
modereta_rewrite_description: The current Modereta is not a patch over the old one. It reorganises the project around independent commands, rules, services and data so new utilities can be added without starting the same fire again.
vsds_customization_description: You stop the server, change settings, roles or mods on the volume and start it up again. The classic way, but tidier.
vsds_code_knows: the server knows who you are
vsds_data_description: Worlds, configuration, players, mods and logs outside the container lifecycle.
vsds_container_description: Server, dependencies, unprivileged user, and startup script in a reproducible environment.
vsds_console_description: You can follow the output, review the log files and connect to the server console to execute commands live.
vsds_code_root: root can stay out of this
vsds_hero_description: Vintage Story Dockerized Server packages the server, its dependencies, and startup logic into versioned images. You choose the version, the port, and where to store the data. Docker takes care of the rest.
vsds_deploy_footer: Name · user · port · data · version. Nothing hidden under the rug.
vsds_idea_description_before: VSDS separates the application from persistent data. The container can be updated, removed, or rebuilt; worlds, players, configurations, mods, and logs remain in the folder you mounted as
vsds_idea_title: The server is replaceable. Your world is not.
vsds_hero_lead: A Vintage Story server. One command. Zero strange rituals.
vsds_security_title: It does not run as root. And that is good news.
vsds_meta_description: VSDS packages Vintage Story servers into versioned Docker images for deploying them with a command and keeping the data outside the container.
vsds_update_tag_description: You choose a specific version or use `stable`, `rc` or `latest`.
vsds_update_start_description: You create the container with the same data path and the server continues where it was.
vsds_update_stop_description: Stop the previous container and remove it. The volume is not touched.
vsds_visible_title: All the important things are in plain sight.
vsds_visible_description: The persistent volume is a normal folder. You can edit `serversettings.json`, add mods in `Mods`, check `Logs`, or make your own copy without entering a black box.
vsl_flow_title: From download to world in three steps.
vsl_backups_description: Manual or automatic backups before playing, with restoration if a world or a configuration decides not to cooperate.
vsl_mods_description: Mod management from within the application, a translatable interface with i18next and automatic launcher updates on startup.
vsl_meta_description: VS Launcher, an unofficial version and installation manager for Vintage Story for Windows and Linux, developed with Electron, React, and TypeScript.
vsl_hero_description: An unofficial launcher designed to install the game, separate worlds, configs and mods, make backups and switch versions without manually moving folders around.
vsl_hero_alt: Main screen of VS Launcher with a Vintage Story installation ready to play
vsl_isolated_description: Each profile retains its own worlds, maps, settings, and mods without mixing with the others.
vsl_hero_lead: Vintage Story, with multiple versions and without turning each installation into an archaeological excavation.
vsl_problem_title: A game. Many ways to play it.
vsl_problem_description: Vintage Story allows very different versions, worlds, and mod collections. The hard part wasn't opening the game: it was keeping everything separate, knowing which installation each thing used, and not breaking a save along the way.
vsl_step_play_description: The launcher prepares the installation, creates the automatic backup if applicable, and opens the game.
vsl_step_installation_description: Create a profile with your own worlds, settings, maps and collection of mods.
vsl_technical_description: The interface was built with Electron, React, and TypeScript. Behind it were downloads, compression and extraction of files, file system operations, semantic version control, automatic updates, and internationalization.
vsl_step_version_description: Download the Vintage Story version you need or register one you already have installed.
xvelte_area_apps_description: Localisation with Paraglide and Tauri integrations, alongside the usual SvelteKit web foundation. It does not live only in a pretty gallery.
vsl_versions_description: Install different versions of Vintage Story with a couple of clicks and update them without repeating the whole process.
xvelte_area_logic_description: Hooks, attachments and utilities for resolving interactions and state without rewriting the same piece in every project.
xvelte_code_title: A component already in the project
xvelte_code_footer: Normal, editable code with no magic hidden on another server.
xvelte_areas_description: xvelte was created to gather the reusable code needed to build real applications: from a button through to interface state, localisation or desktop integration.
xvelte_demo_description: The components on this page are xvelte too. Self-referential, but usefully so.
xvelte_area_visual_description: Tokens, light and dark themes, global styles and semantic icons that maintain a common language without tying the design.
xvelte_idea_description_2: You can change the structure, styles, dependencies or behaviour without waiting for a new package option. In return, you are also responsible for what you copy. Freedom, with an instruction manual. Fair enough.
xvelte_hero_lead: The pieces I always ended up building again. Now they all live in the same drawer.
xvelte_hero_description: A personal collection of components, hooks, attachments, styles and utilities for building interfaces with SvelteKit. Copy them into your project, adapt them and they become yours. No need to wrestle with someone else's API to move three pixels.
xvelte_hero_alt: Screenshot of the xvelte documentation home page
xvelte_meta_description: xvelte is a personal collection of reusable components, hooks, attachments, styles, and utilities for building applications and websites with SvelteKit.
xvelte_preferences_description: A small sample, not a full application packed into a card.
xvelte_idea_title: Copying is not the last resort. It is the model.
xvelte_step_adapt_description: Adapt the code to the application without getting trapped in an API designed for everyone.
xvelte_real_title: Made for projects, not for an eternal demo.
xvelte_idea_description_1: There is no package with a rigid API, no component registry and no CLI. You choose a stable version, copy only what you need and that code becomes part of the application.
xvelte_step_choose_description: Start from a stable release and review the guide for the piece you are going to use.
xvelte_real_description: The same foundation works for websites, internal dashboards, Electron or Tauri applications and highly interactive interfaces. The documentation site is the test bed; real software is the destination.
xvelte_step_copy_description: Add to the project the component and the specific dependencies it needs.
vsds_origin_description: Images prepared and tagged for each compatible server version.
xvelte_area_components_description: Composite primitives and interfaces for forms, navigation, data, multimedia, messaging, and desktop tools.
vsds_security_description: In Linux, the container maps the internal user's UID and GID to those of the local user. This way, it can read and write to the volume without running with root privileges and without leaving a folder full of files that you later cannot touch.
aser_hero_lead: Train, find your path and get started. Without getting lost on the website first.
vsds_folder_label: Usual structure of the VSDS data folder
services_meta_title: Software development and IT services | XurxoMF
services_meta_description: Web development, online stores, bespoke software and IT support for businesses and individuals in Galicia and remotely.
services_title: Development and IT support, taken equally seriously.
services_description: I can build the tool you need or fix the one already in front of you. Web and software development, automation and IT support for businesses and individuals, explained clearly and without the smoke and mirrors.
service_page_includes_title: A complete service, without creatively small print.
service_page_process_description: Scope, timing and decisions are clear from the outset. If something is not worth your money, I will tell you that too.
service_process_step_1_description: You explain the problem, context and outcome you need. I ask what matters, not questions for the sport of it.
service_process_step_2_description: I define scope, technology, priorities, timing and cost in language that does not need translating from IT.
service_process_step_3_title: I build and keep you informed
service_process_step_3_description: I work in stages, share progress and confirm important decisions with you before building further.
service_process_step_4_description: I test that everything works, explain what you need and make any sensible follow-up support or maintenance clear.
service_page_examples_title: Examples of what I can solve.
service_page_examples_description: Every situation differs, but these are useful examples of the work covered by this service.
service_area_development: I work remotely with businesses and individuals in Galicia and anywhere else. Meetings can be online or in person around Salvaterra de Miño when the project needs it.
service_area_it: I provide remote and on-site support in Salvaterra de Miño, Salceda de Caselas, Vigo, O Porriño, Tui, Ponteareas and other parts of southern Galicia.
service_web_short: Fast, accessible corporate websites, landing pages and platforms designed to produce useful results.
service_web_meta_description: Bespoke web development for businesses and professionals in Galicia: corporate websites, landing pages and fast, accessible platforms.
service_web_lead: I build websites that explain what you do, load quickly and help turn a visit into an enquiry, booking or sale.
service_web_problem: A slow, confusing, outdated or uneditable website loses trust and opportunities. Looking good is not enough; it needs to help the business.
service_web_audience: Businesses, professionals and projects that need a new website, a proper rebuild or a specific web tool without forcing everything into a generic theme.
service_web_includes_1: Content architecture and journeys designed around your audience.
service_web_includes_3: Development with SvelteKit, WordPress or the technology that genuinely fits.
service_web_includes_4: Basic technical SEO, analytics, forms, deployment and a clear handover.
service_web_example_1: A corporate website that organises services, real work and contact routes to turn visitors into useful enquiries.
service_web_example_2: A platform with manageable content, search, forms or specialist areas that a generic landing page cannot cover.
service_web_faq_1_question: How much does a website cost?
service_web_faq_1_answer: It depends on page count, features, content and whether a design already exists. Before giving a fixed figure, I review the scope and separate what is essential from what can wait.
service_web_faq_2_question: Will I be able to update the content?
service_web_faq_2_answer: Yes. Where needed, I provide a clear management area or use a CMS. If the website rarely changes, we can also avoid adding an admin panel merely for the sake of having one.
service_web_faq_3_question: Do you include the domain, hosting and SEO?
service_web_faq_3_answer: I can configure the domain, email, hosting, deployment and technical SEO foundation. Third-party provider fees remain separate and the accounts stay in your name.
service_ecommerce_short: E-commerce with a clear catalogue, reliable payments and day-to-day management that does not require a developer for every change.
service_ecommerce_meta_description: Online stores built with Shopify, WooCommerce or bespoke solutions for businesses selling products and services from Galicia.
service_ecommerce_lead: I build and improve online stores so finding, understanding and buying a product — and managing the resulting order — is straightforward for both sides.
service_ecommerce_problem: A catalogue without structure, a confusing checkout or awkward administration turns every sale into a small obstacle course.
service_ecommerce_audience: Brands, retailers and businesses that want to begin selling online, migrate an existing store or bring order to a catalogue that grew without a plan.
service_ecommerce_includes_1: Catalogue structure, collections, filters and navigation.
service_ecommerce_includes_2: Payments, shipping, taxes and transactional email configuration.
service_ecommerce_includes_3: Design and development with Shopify, WooCommerce or a bespoke solution.
service_ecommerce_includes_4: Initial catalogue work, analytics, training and preparation for daily management.
service_ecommerce_example_1: A brand selling a small catalogue through a carefully designed identity and a direct purchasing journey.
service_ecommerce_example_2: A distributor with a broad catalogue, product families, documentation and recurring professional orders.
service_ecommerce_faq_1_answer: It depends on the catalogue, budget, integrations and who will manage the store. I recommend the option that reduces medium-term problems, not whichever platform is fashionable that week.
service_ecommerce_faq_2_question: Can you migrate my existing store?
service_ecommerce_faq_2_answer: Yes. I review products, customers, orders, URLs, content and integrations before preparing a checked migration with redirects, so information and search visibility are protected.
service_ecommerce_faq_3_answer: We can agree a complete initial upload, an import, or a structure and training for your team to continue. It is defined before the work is priced.
service_custom_software_short: Internal tools, platforms and integrations built around the way your business actually works.
service_custom_software_meta_description: Bespoke software development for businesses: internal tools, platforms, integrations and solutions for specialist processes.
service_custom_software_lead: When a spreadsheet is crying for help and generic tools force the business to adapt around them, I design software around the real process.
service_custom_software_problem: Duplicating data, copying information between tools and relying on manual processes creates errors, wastes time and makes it hard to know what is happening.
service_custom_software_audience: Businesses and teams with a specialist process that does not fit a standard product, or systems that need connecting because they currently ignore each other.
service_custom_software_includes_1: Analysis of the current process, users, permissions and data.
service_custom_software_includes_2: A prototype and definition of a useful first version.
service_custom_software_includes_3: Development of the platform, dashboard, API or integrations required.
service_custom_software_includes_4: Testing, deployment, documentation and later evolution.
service_custom_software_example_1: An internal dashboard centralising customers, tasks, documents and statuses currently scattered across email and spreadsheets.
service_custom_software_example_2: An integration that keeps services in sync and removes the need to copy information by hand every day.
service_custom_software_faq_1_question: Does everything need building from scratch?
service_custom_software_faq_1_answer: Not always. I first check whether an existing product, integration or small bespoke layer solves the problem. Building software for its own sake is an expensive way to decorate a CV.
service_custom_software_faq_2_question: Can we begin with a small version?
service_custom_software_faq_2_answer: Yes, and that is often the sensible route. We define a first version that solves the core problem and prioritise everything else for later development based on real use.
service_custom_software_faq_3_answer: We agree whether you need occasional support, a bank of hours or ongoing maintenance from the outset. Code, documentation and access are prepared so the system is not a black box.
service_apps_short: Mobile and desktop applications that put a service, process or product on the right device.
service_apps_meta_description: Mobile and desktop application development for Android, iOS, Windows, Linux and macOS, tailored to your project.
service_apps_lead: I build mobile and desktop applications that make proper use of the device without turning every platform into an entirely separate project.
service_apps_problem: A website cannot always cover offline work, operating-system integration, notifications, local files or an intensive day-to-day experience.
service_apps_audience: Businesses, professionals and products that need an application for customers, internal teams or a community across Android, iOS, Windows, Linux or macOS.
service_apps_includes_1: Platform selection, use cases and first-version scope.
service_apps_includes_2: A responsive interface consistent with the system and brand.
service_apps_includes_3: Integration with APIs, accounts, files, notifications or device features.
service_apps_includes_4: Packaging, testing, publishing or distribution, and update support.
service_apps_example_1: A desktop application managing installations, files and updates without requiring people to work from a terminal.
service_apps_example_2: A mobile app for checking information, receiving alerts and completing tasks away from the office.
service_apps_faq_1_answer: It depends on features, performance and target platforms. A shared foundation avoids duplicated cost when it suits the product; where a feature requires native code, I do not force it through an abstraction.
service_apps_faq_2_question: Do you also publish to app stores?
service_apps_faq_2_answer: I can prepare builds, listings and the publication process. Apple, Google or Microsoft accounts should remain in the client's name and their fees are billed directly.
service_apps_faq_3_answer: Yes, if the use case requires it. We need to define what is stored, how it synchronises and what happens when conflicting changes meet after connectivity returns.
service_automation_short: Bots, scripts and integrations that remove repetitive work and connect services that currently do not speak.
service_automation_meta_description: Discord bots, scripts, API integrations and bespoke automation for businesses, teams and online communities.
service_automation_lead: I automate repetitive work and build bots that respond, moderate, notify or coordinate processes without a person acting as a bridge all day.
service_automation_problem: Copying data, checking events manually or repeating the same action daily consumes time and lets mistakes appear at precisely the least helpful moment.
service_automation_audience: Businesses with repetitive processes, teams connecting several tools, and communities needing Discord or Telegram bots with their own behaviour.
service_automation_includes_1: Analysis of the task, rules, exceptions and permissions.
service_automation_includes_2: Discord or Telegram bots, scripts and API integrations.
service_automation_includes_3: Activity logs, alerts, error handling and manual controls.
service_automation_example_1: A Discord bot managing commands, favourites, automatic alerts and community-specific rules.
service_automation_example_2: A process collecting data from an API, transforming it and alerting the team only when something needs attention.
service_automation_faq_1_question: Can you build a private Discord bot?
service_automation_faq_1_answer: Yes. It can be limited to one server and use commands, menus, events, permissions and a database according to what the community or team needs.
service_automation_faq_2_question: Can an automation break when an API changes?
service_automation_faq_2_answer: It can. That is why I prepare logging, alerts and error handling, and explain the maintenance needed when external services may change.
service_automation_faq_3_answer: It is not always worthwhile. The task must be repetitive and stable enough. If automation costs more than the time it saves, the honest answer is not to build it.
service_it_short: Remote and on-site diagnosis, repair and IT support for businesses and individuals.
service_it_meta_description: IT technician in Salvaterra de Miño providing on-site support in Vigo, O Porriño, Tui, Ponteareas, Salceda and southern Galicia.
service_it_lead: I solve problems with computers, software, networks and devices through clear remote support or a visit to your home or business.
service_it_problem: A slow computer, vanishing printer, failing application or unstable network can stop a home or business over a problem whose solution is sometimes considerably less dramatic.
service_it_audience: Individuals, freelancers and businesses needing diagnosis, repair, configuration or help making an informed IT decision instead of buying parts at random.
service_it_includes_1: Diagnosis of slow computers, errors, startup issues, software and peripherals.
service_it_includes_2: Installation and configuration of systems, software, printers and devices.
service_it_includes_3: Cleaning, upgrades, backups, recovery and data migration where viable.
service_it_includes_4: Remote assistance or on-site visits to homes and businesses in the service area.
service_it_example_1: A computer that has slowed down, fails to start or needs its data moving to a new machine without leaving half a life behind.
service_it_example_2: A workstation with poorly configured email, printer, applications and backups that needs to be left working and understood.
service_it_faq_1_question: Do you visit homes and businesses?
service_it_faq_1_answer: Yes. I provide on-site support in Salvaterra de Miño, Salceda de Caselas, Vigo, O Porriño, Tui, Ponteareas and nearby areas. Travel and any distance-based charge are confirmed beforehand.
service_it_faq_2_question: Can you solve the problem remotely?
service_it_faq_2_answer: Many software, configuration and account issues can be resolved remotely. Hardware, cabling or a computer that will not start generally requires an in-person visit.
service_it_faq_3_question: Do you charge if the computer is beyond repair?
service_it_faq_3_answer: Diagnosis and travel are work even when a repair is not worthwhile. Before replacing parts or spending more time, I explain the options so you can make an informed decision.
service_it_maintenance_short: Preventive maintenance and ongoing support so a business's computers do not live permanently in emergency mode.
service_it_maintenance_meta_description: Business IT maintenance in Salvaterra de Miño and southern Galicia: computers, networks, backups, updates and support.
service_it_maintenance_lead: I keep computers, software, networks and backups under control to reduce incidents and respond with context when one appears.
service_it_maintenance_problem: Dealing with IT only when everything stops is expensive: updates accumulate, backups go unchecked, computers lack order and access depends on one person's memory.
service_it_maintenance_audience: Freelancers, offices and small businesses that do not need their own IT department but do need someone who knows their systems and provides continuity.
service_it_maintenance_includes_1: A basic inventory, condition review and priorities for each computer.
service_it_maintenance_includes_2: Updates, security, users, software and routine configuration.
service_it_maintenance_includes_3: Backups, checks and guidance for recovering information.
service_it_maintenance_includes_4: Remote support, agreed visits and incident follow-up.
service_it_maintenance_example_1: A small office needing regular checks of computers, accounts, backups and networking instead of waiting for the next failure.
service_it_maintenance_example_2: A business with one point of contact for incidents, new workstations and documentation of important configurations.
service_it_maintenance_faq_1_question: Does maintenance require a monthly fee?
service_it_maintenance_faq_1_answer: It can be a subscription, a bank of hours or scheduled reviews. The right model depends on computer count and actual support needs; there is no point paying for cover you do not need.
service_it_maintenance_faq_2_answer: I prioritise incidents for maintenance clients according to our agreement, but I do not sell imaginary 24/7 coverage. Hours and response times are clear before the service begins.
service_it_maintenance_faq_3_question: Do you also maintain websites and online stores?
service_it_maintenance_faq_3_answer: Yes, but I separate that from computer maintenance because the work and risks differ. We can combine both in a clear proposal rather than hiding everything in one mysterious invoice line.
